Definition: apparently a primary word; a lamb:--lamb.
BiblicalUsage: John the Baptist saw Jesus coming and said, 'Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.' The Ethiopian eunuch was reading Isaiah's picture of the same lamb — led to the slaughter, silent before his shearer — and Philip showed him it was Jesus. Peter says we were redeemed not with silver and gold but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the lamb is the whole gospel in one word: innocent, offered, and enough. Every lamb in the Old Testament pointed forward to this one, and this one Lamb takes away the sin of the world — not just Israel's sin, and not just mine, but the world's. That is why I can rest: the sacrifice is finished, and the Lamb lives.
